chunks: From him, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I buy something with dirhams, and give the shortfall as one or two grains [of gold].' He said, 'No, until you specify it.' Then he said, 'Unless it is like these clear dirhams that are with us in whole numbers [i.e., exact multiples without remainder].'

key_terms.الْحَبَّةَ: A grain (unit of weight for gold)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on paying a debt with a fractional amount of a different currency?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the principle of avoiding *gharar* (uncertainty) in currency exchange by requiring precise specification when the amount is not an integer, unless the coins are 'clear' (*awdahiyyah*) whole units that divide evenly. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on financial clarity and fairness, ensuring that fractional payments are explicitly defined to prevent disputes in commercial transactions.
